messages:
lisa: Heads-up — noticed a repro where a user in org B can list keys in org A after the RBAC refactor. sending logs.
ajit: ack. can you paste the exact steps? sounds like a role attachment bug after the affinity change.
lisa: repro steps:
```
# curl as user from org-b
GET /v1/projects/org-a/keys
Authorization: Bearer <org-b-user-token>
```
response: 200 with key metadata. expected 403.
maya: who owns the PR that touched org affinity mapping? i saw a refactor last week that normalized org aliases.
sam: that was PR #1729 (role-mapper: normalize workspace aliases). i raised a question but it merged after approvals.
lisa: logs show the request passes workspace-alias header "x-workspace" => "org-b", but the internal resolution maps alias -> canonical org via alias_index. alias_index lookup returned the canonical org id "org-a" for that alias. weird.
ajit: that suggests alias_index may have been superseded by the global alias fallback introduced in the PR. @sam can you check the mapper logic?
sam: looking now. in role-mapper we added fallbackResolve(alias) that falls back to first matching org if exact match fails. i can see how a fuzzy match could return org-a for a partially similar alias.
lisa: reproduction payload attached in logs: "x-workspace: org-b-prod" returned "org-a" canonical because of a substring match. not intended.
security-bot: Automated alert triggered: anomalous cross-org access pattern detected. Confidence 0.83.
maya: urgent: rollback candidate? if this lets org-B users enumerate org-A keys that's high-sev.
ajit: can we add a quick guard: block any fallbackResolve result where the request's token org != resolved canonical org unless token has cross-org role? i.e. enforce token-org equality before applying role mapping.
sam: quick patch prepared. adding explicit check in auth middleware:
```
if (token.org != canonicalOrg && !token.roles.contains('cross-org')) {
  deny();
}
```
will push as hotfix to staging then prod if green.
lisa: good. also need to check audit logs to identify range of impacted requests. i'll run a query:
```
SELECT * FROM audit_events
WHERE resource_type='key' AND event IN ('list','get')
AND actor_org <> resource_org
AND timestamp > '2024-02-20';
```
sam: deploying hotfix to staging now.
ops-bot: deploy started for commit 9f3a2b (role-mapper hotfix) by sam. CI: green.
sam: staging tests: repro no longer returns 200 for org-b token. returns 403 as expected. moving to prod in 10.
security-bot: detected additional sessions matching pattern; created ticket SEC-3421.
ajit: post-deploy: run account-level audit to enumerate affected service accounts and rotate any long-lived keys that were exposed.
lisa: i've exported list of actors from audit query, 18 distinct actors, mostly service-accounts used by integrations. starting rotate plan.
maya: notify affected customers? product/legal input required. tagging @product and @legal.
sam: prod deploy complete. quick smoke checks OK.
lisa: thanks. follow-ups: 1) revert fallbackResolve design (or restrict it behind opt-in), 2) unit tests for alias matching edge cases, 3) improve telemetry on alias resolution decisions, 4) customer notification draft.
ajit: create postmortem ticket and link to SEC-3421. also add regression test to nightly e2e.
lisa: draft of customer notification in #security-commms: "We observed and mitigated a short-lived permission mapping issue..." — will share for review.
maya: good work. main deliverable: ship rollback or tighten semantics, rotate keys, notify, add tests. thanks everyone :thumbsup
